steps.title: Why collaborating in the cloud is smarter
steps.body: Instead of emailing a document back and forth, tools like Google Docs or Word Online let you work in the same file at the same time as others. Changes show up instantly, and you can see who changed what.

steps.title: Using version history
steps.body: Accidentally deleted or overwritten something? Via File > Version history (Google Docs) you can view and restore an earlier version. No more need to keep separate backup files.

steps.title: Organizing folders smartly
steps.body: Use shared folders for projects you work on with others, and keep your personal files separate. Consistent naming (date + subject) saves you a lot of searching later.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Create a new document in Google Drive below and check out the sharing and version-history options.

lessons.title: Backing up and securing your phone

steps.title: Setting up automatic backup
steps.body: Turn on automatic backup for photos, contacts, and app data (Android: Settings > System > Backup; iPhone: Settings > [your name] > iCloud). This way you won't lose everything if your phone is lost or stolen.

steps.title: Finding or wiping your phone remotely
steps.body: Turn on 'Find My Device' (Android) or 'Find My iPhone' (Apple). If lost or stolen, you can use this to see its location, make it ring, or remotely wipe all data.

steps.title: Screen lock and updates
steps.body: Use a PIN, pattern, or biometric lock — never 'no lock'. Install software updates as soon as possible: they often close security gaps.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Check on your own phone whether automatic backup and 'find my phone' are turned on.

lessons.title: Managing subscriptions and your digital budget

steps.title: Creeping subscription costs
steps.body: Streaming services, apps, cloud storage — subscriptions add up quickly without you noticing. Periodically (every quarter, say) review your bank statement for recurring payments you no longer use.

steps.title: Canceling subscriptions
steps.body: For an app-store subscription (Apple/Google): go to your account settings > Subscriptions to see what's active and cancel it. Don't forget free trials — set a reminder before they automatically convert to a paid subscription.

steps.title: Budgeting apps
steps.body: Many banking apps (or standalone apps) can automatically categorize your spending, so you can see at a glance where your money goes. Handy for staying in control without tracking everything manually.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Check your active subscriptions in your phone's settings and see if there's anything you no longer use.

lessons.title: Making a password manager a daily habit

steps.title: Why this should be a habit by now
steps.body: As we saw in the Safety module: a password manager isn't an extra step anymore, it's a basic habit — like a toothbrush. It remembers, generates, and auto-fills your passwords.

steps.title: Everything in one place
steps.body: Besides passwords, a password manager often lets you store bank details, ID documents, and secure notes — encrypted, and accessible only with your master password.

steps.title: Sharing with family
steps.body: Most password managers offer a family plan that lets you securely share passwords (like a streaming account), without literally texting the password to someone.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: If you don't use a password manager yet: install one today and set it up for your most important account.
